title: Rabbi Abba bar Yasa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 4:8, the statement is reported in the name of Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman proposes the reading “Rabbi Ba, Rabbi Yasa, in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,” as in Sanhedrin 1:4.

notes.text: Hyman’s proposal removes the patronymic bar between Abba/Ba and Yasa. The internal relation between the two named transmitters in his abbreviated wording remains open, so no additional “in the name of” is invented between them.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Sanhedrin 4:8 paragraph reads Ba bar Yasa in Yochanan’s name; the parallel 1:4 reads Ba, Yasa, in Yochanan’s name. These directly support Hyman’s textual contrast. No connector is supplied between Ba and Yasa, and the formal difference does not establish a new relationship or genealogy.

In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 4:8 has Ba bar Yasa, while 1:4 places Ba and Yasa side by side before “in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.” Hyman explains in his separate entry on Rabbi Abba bar Yosef (vol. I, p. 47) that he understands the two rabbis to have both said it in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.
